learningObjective: Given a small IR fragment, identify which classical optimization (constant folding, CSE, DCE) is applied and confirm semantic preservation.

canonicalClaims.claim: Constant folding evaluates compile-time-known operand computations; CSE merges syntactically equivalent pure computations on identical operands; DCE removes values with no consumer and no observable side effect. All three are semantics-preserving on pure IR fragments.
conditions: Operations involved are pure (no side effects).
Operand equality is decidable syntactically or via value numbering.
nonImplications: Does not imply CSE can span arbitrarily large scopes; passes typically operate within a function or basic block group.
Does not imply DCE can remove any unused op — side-effecting ops (e.g., I/O, atomics) are preserved.

misconceptions.claim: SSA form prohibits a single value from being used more than once, so CSE would create SSA violations.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SSA requires single-definition, not single-use; a value can have arbitrarily many uses.

misconceptions.claim: DCE is unsafe because removing any operation might violate side-effect ordering.
misconceptions.whyWrong: DCE removes only pure, unused ops; side-effecting ops are marked as always live.

misconceptions.claim: Constant folding requires both operands to be numerical literals; folding a symbolic constant like `%c6` requires a separate propagation pass.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Constant folding operates on any operation whose operands' compile-time values are known; those may come from prior folds or propagation.

misconceptions.claim: CSE and constant folding must be applied in a fixed order; running CSE before folding is incorrect.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The two passes are typically iterated to a fixed point; either order eventually converges.

implementationFacts: LLVM: `-instcombine`, `-gvn`, `-dce`, `-adce` implement variants of these optimizations.
MLIR: canonicalization patterns include folding, CSE (`-cse`), and DCE.
performanceScenarios: In graph-level tensor IR, constant folding subsumes 'freezing' weights into computed tensors.
